title: Do a dozen codebook codes predict better than bag-of-words when labels are scarce?
summary: On GoEmotions comments (predict a negative-emotion label, AUC on 1,500 held-out items), a logistic model on 12 word-list codebook codes plus log length beats bag-of-words at every labelling budget from 25 to 1,600 items: 0.65 against 0.56 AUC at 100 labels and 0.75 against 0.67 at 1,600, with bag-of-words still gaining. Adding the codes to the bag of words lands between the two, and a 64-dimension random projection of the words is near chance (0.55 at 1,600). The codes are word lists, not an LLM, and a learned sentence embedding was not tested; one corpus, one label, 12 subsets per size.
lede: do a dozen codebook codes predict better than bag-of-words when labels are scarce? On GoEmotions, 12 word-list codes reached 0.65 AUC at 100 labels against 0.56 for bag-of-words, and still led at 1,600 (0.75 against 0.67). Word lists, not an LLM; no learned embedding tested.
